evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The entry preserves two received Shuowen formulations: “助也。从口，从又” and “手口相助也。从又，从口.” This documents variation within the textual tradition, not the graph’s original construction.
evidence.title: A00483 右 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: 字源字形 / catalogued script forms
evidence.text: The page catalogs an oracle-bone specimen as 鐵7.4 合20836, early Western Zhou bronze forms including 夨令方彝, and later Chu, Qin-slip, Shuowen seal, and clerical forms. This is a sequence of catalog labels, not a verified dated sequence or proof of the graph’s earliest sense.
evidence.title: 右 yòu - 汉典

evidence.source: 普及版 字通, via Kotobank
evidence.field: 右 字形 / 形聲與語義說明
evidence.text: This account analyzes 又 as a right hand and 口 as a ritual prayer vessel, associating the graph with ritual service and later assistance. It rejects the Shuowen/Duan hand-and-mouth explanation as the original formation. This is a competing interpretation; it does not establish that 口 was merely a differentiating mark.
evidence.title: 右(ウ)とは？ 意味や使い方 - コトバンク

evidence.text: The entry separately records helping, blessing or protection, right hand and side, west, rank, and banquet-related urging of food, with citations to classical works. Those citations are not independently dated first attestations and do not establish a chronological semantic chain among these senses.
evidence.title: 右 yòu - 汉典

evidence.source: 普及版 字通, via Kotobank
evidence.field: 聲系 / graph versus sound component
evidence.text: This account describes 又 as the initial graph and treats 右, 佑, and 祐 as later phonetic-semantic graphs in a related word family. It does not support calling 又 a phonetic component inside 右. Whole-graph use of 又 and an internal phonetic-component analysis are distinct claims.

evidence.text: The exact page labels the file a vector depiction of 右 in oracle-script style, lists several paleographic databases as sources, and states that the image is public domain. It is a modern digital redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph. The page’s original-file link resolves to https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/33/%E5%8F%B3-oracle.svg, but the web tool failed to fetch that image during this invocation.

gaps: No primary paleographic image or dated original inscription was visually inspected in this invocation. The disputed accounts—又 as an earlier right-hand graph with later differentiating 口, versus a meaningful ritual/prayer construction—remain unresolved.

The local Unihan and Baxter–Sagart rows included in the input were not independently fetched from their upstream pages in this invocation. They remain local-data readings and do not prove a phonetic role; no external claim here depends on them.

Dictionary entries list directional, helping, blessing/protection, rank, west, and banquet-related uses, but earliest Chinese attestations and semantic links remain unestablished; gloss order is not chronology.
The Shuowen formulations differ in component order, but no critical manuscript witness was examined to determine whether textual corruption explains the difference.

No usable historical glyph image is proposed: Commons oracle original-file fetch failed, big-seal and oracle candidates are excluded by prior failed-image records, and Xiaoxuetang returned 401 in the supplied query record.

limitations.text: No available image passed the required access and provenance checks in this invocation: the oracle image’s exact Commons page supports its modern redraw status and public-domain terms, but fetching its linked original failed; the other listed candidates are unavailable from prior 404 findings, and Xiaoxuetang was unavailable with HTTP 401.
